title: Qutb Minar
blurb: The 72.5 m victory tower of the Delhi Sultanate, begun 1199: five fluted storeys of red sandstone and marble with Quranic inscription bands, ringed by the Qutb complex.

sourceUrls.label: UNESCO: Qutb Minar and its Monuments

systems.name: Tower storeys
systems.description: The five tapering storeys: shafts and facing, red and buff sandstone below, marble and sandstone above.

systems.name: Fluted skins
systems.description: The fluted outer skins: alternating on the first storey, rounded on the second, angular on the third.

systems.name: Inscription bands
systems.description: Bands of carved Quranic inscriptions in Arabic and Nagari scripts on each storey.

systems.name: Balconies
systems.description: The five projecting balconies with decorated brackets and railings separating the storeys.

systems.name: Base and entrance
systems.description: Plinth, mouldings, entrance door, arch and steps.

systems.name: Crown
systems.description: The crown pavilion ring, parapet, cupola plinth, and the removed 19th-century cupola on the lawns.

systems.name: Iron Pillar
systems.description: The 7.02 m wrought-iron pillar famed for resisting corrosion.

systems.name: Qutb complex
systems.description: The Quwwat-ul-Islam prayer-hall screen, cloisters, Alai Darwaza and the tomb of Iltutmish.
